Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation / capacity uplift

Karthik,

Thanks for the run-through earlier. We're getting close on our side but need clarity on two items before moving to procurement:

1) Price hold: can Redwood hold current tiered pricing for 12 months if we sign a multi-year agreement? That helps us lock in economics while we ramp.
2) Credits/true-up: we're expecting a meaningful uplift in Q3; we need a mechanism for true-up credits if usage spikes above committed volumes.

Also, procurement asked if a 3-year commitment window is possible with a slightly larger discount (they mentioned 10% in principle). Could you outline options you can put on the table?

Sam
Director, AI Platforms
Atlas Retail

Subject: Renewal proposal: 2-year & 3-year options with tiered uplift and true-up credits

Sam — attaching a concise summary and an MAP so procurement can see milestones. High level options (examples, USD-equivalent token pricing):

Option A — 2-year (preferred):
- Year 1: price hold at current effective rates for 12 months.
- Year 2: modest 5% list rate uplift (we keep committed unit price flat for committed volume).
- Credits: one-time onboarding credit = $35k; true-up credit bucket = 5% of annual commit to be applied to overages in Q3/Q4 if usage exceeds committed volumes.
- Capacity ramp schedule: 0–3 months: baseline; months 4–12: +40% capacity; months 13–24: steady-state.

Option B — 3-year (deeper commit):
- Year 1: price hold with a 7% up-front discount on committed units.
- Years 2–3: graduated pricing with annual step-ups capped at 6%/year.
- Credits: onboarding credit = $50k; increased true-up bucket = 7% of annual commit.
- Optional guaranteed burst pool for seasonal peaks at reduced burst rate.

Operational notes:
- We can add a contractual true-up clause with a defined formula (committed vs actual usage, applied credits, invoicing cadence).
- SLA: standard Redwood SLA applies; we can include a one-time SLA credit in the event of a major outage tied to the renewal.

Attachments: [Attachment: renewal_summary_v1.pdf (PDF, 48 KB)] [Attachment: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (XLSX, 22 KB)]

If procurement prefers 3-year with Net30 invoicing, we can present a blended discount table. If you like, I can route a draft amendment to legal and procurement to accelerate review (DocuSign-ready).

Next steps: 1) Let me know which option (A vs B) aligns with Atlas’s runway. 2) Provide procurement contact and PO cadence. 3) We’ll prepare an amendment + MAP for signature.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts

Counter-OPT (middle ground):
- Term: 3 years.
- Year 1: price hold; 6% up-front discount on committed units (applied to first 12 months).
- Years 2–3: blended step-ups capped at 5% per year.
- Credits: one-time sign-on credit = $45k (applied to first invoice); true-up bucket = 6% of annual committed spend for overage offsets.
- Burst pool: guaranteed seasonal burst pool (pre-provisioned capacity) at 60% of standard burst rate for up to 12 hours/month during Q4 holiday windows.
- Payment: Net30 OK. We accept PO pre-signature; DocuSign + PO is the normal flow for Atlas.
- Docs: we will send amendment + W-9 + insurance cert in separate email; legal is ready to accept quick redlines on the incumbent terms doc.
